# Planned follow-up: complete editor i18n migration

The vue-i18n framework is **wired and live** in the editor as of this
release. The infrastructure pieces are in place:

- `src/i18n/index.ts` — `createI18n` setup, locale detection from
  `navigator.language` + `localStorage` persistence under
  `parallax-editor:locale`, `setLocale(...)` helper.
- `src/locales/{es,en}.ts` — message dictionaries. Spanish is the source of
  truth; English mirrors its structure.
- `src/components/ui/LanguageSwitcher.vue` — drop-down rendered in the
  workspace selector header.
- Default locale: `es` (preserves the current UX for existing users).

What is **NOT** yet done is the per-string migration of the existing
hardcoded Spanish UI to `$t()` / `useI18n()` calls. The strings are
distributed across ~50 components and ~hundreds of literal references; the
E2E suite locks the visible text in for regression checks, so the
migration needs to land in coordinated chunks.

This PR ships the framework so future PRs can migrate by area without
re-doing the wiring.

## Migration plan (suggested order by visibility)

1. **Workspace selector** — `src/views/ProjectSelector.vue`,
   `src/components/selector/ProjectCard.vue`. First screen the user sees.
2. **Top toolbar** — `src/components/toolbar/*.vue` (buttons, tooltips,
   tab labels, menus).
3. **Layers panel** — `src/components/layers/*.vue` (panel header, action
   buttons, drag/drop hints, insertion-line labels).
4. **Claude panel** — `src/components/claude/ClaudePanel.vue` (chat
   placeholder, send button, error/success messages).
5. **Doctor screen** — `src/components/doctor/DoctorHost.vue`.
6. **Properties panel** — `src/components/properties/*.vue`. **Largest**
   chunk. Group titles first, then field labels per section
   (size/position, animation, theme, custom-component props, etc.).
7. **Git / publish panel** — `src/components/git/*.vue`.
8. **Stores + composables** — `confirm(...)` / `alert(...)` strings in
   `src/stores/{editor,workspaces}.ts`, `src/composables/*.ts`. These need
   the `t` function from `useI18n()` imported in each module.
9. **Server-side user-facing errors** — `server/api.ts`, `server/git.ts`,
   `server/sfcBundler.ts`. These currently respond with Spanish error
   strings; for full i18n we'd need either to send error CODES + translate
   in the client, OR to negotiate locale via an `Accept-Language` header.
   The former is the cleaner long-term shape.

## How to migrate one component

1. Identify the literal strings in `<template>` and `<script>`.
2. Pick a key namespace based on the file path
   (e.g. `toolbar.zoom.in`, `properties.size.width`).
3. Add the keys to `src/locales/es.ts` (with the existing Spanish copy)
   and `src/locales/en.ts` (with the English translation).
4. In the SFC, add `import { useI18n } from 'vue-i18n'` and
   `const { t } = useI18n()` at the top of `<script setup>`.
5. Replace literals: `"Eliminar"` → `t('common.delete')` in script,
   `{{ t('common.delete') }}` in template, `:title="t('common.delete')"`
   in attributes.
6. Re-run `yarn test:e2e`. The E2E suite checks text against the **default
   locale (Spanish)**, so as long as your `es.ts` keys match the old
   literals, the tests stay green.
7. Verify the EN translation works by flipping the language switcher in
   the workspace selector.

## Tooling

Consider adding to a future PR:

- [`vue-i18n-extract`](https://github.com/Spittal/vue-i18n-extract) — lint
  CI step that fails on missing keys / unused keys.
- Eslint rule (`@intlify/vue-i18n/no-raw-text`) to flag hardcoded text in
  templates.

## Coverage target

- 100% of template literals migrated.
- 100% of `confirm(...)` / `alert(...)` / `console.warn` user-facing
  messages migrated.
- Server error CODES instead of literal strings (a separate, larger
  refactor — could ship after the client-side migration).
